title: PR follow-through action catalog
content:
Purpose:
Quick, portable catalog of concrete follow-through actions after merging PRs. Goal is to avoid the typical “we'll circle back” black hole — capture small, measurable followups and assign them immediately (or schedule). This is a personal scratchpad that I use when triaging merged work; will refine into a small bot checklist later.

How to use (two-minute process):
1) After merge, open this doc and copy the relevant sections into the PR comment or create a short follow-up ticket.
2) If action is >2dev-days, create a Jira (RD- prefix) and assign an owner.
3) If action is tiny (docs update, lint, minor test flake), tag as "quick" and do in the next sprint grooming slot.

Triage matrix (quick heuristic):
- Severity (S): S0 = production outage; S1 = visible incorrectness for customers; S2 = performance regressions or noisy logs; S3 = cosmetic docs/cleanup.
- Blast radius (B): small = one route/module, medium = service-level, large = cross-service / infra.
- Default follow-up action mapping:
  - S0 or B=large -> immediate rollback + postmortem ticket (owner: approver + oncall).
  - S1 + B=medium -> hotfix PR or canary rollback; create RD ticket and tag eng-sre.
  - S2 -> create performance investigation ticket; include baseline and current metrics.
  - S3 -> backlog grooming item, low priority.

Action catalog (concrete items to copy into PR comment or ticket):
- Observability additions:
  - Add per-route latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) to the model-route dashboard for 24h post-deploy. (owner: @owner-ops)
  - Add a dedicated error tag for this PR in logs (e.g., "pr:4582") so we can filter.
  - Create a short grafana panel that compares pre/post qps and token-rate.

- Testing / QA follow-ups:
  - Add a unit test case for the edge input that caused the fallback in staging. Attach sample input.
  - Add an integration smoke that exercises the new code path for 3k tokens scenario.
  - Add a fuzz test in fuzz-suite with the new prompt templates.

- Docs / SDKs / Examples:
  - Update quickstart snippet in docs to show new API param.
  - Add a one-line note in changelog with link to PR and the main behavioral change.
  - Notify SDK owners if public surface changed; propose deprecation window if needed.

- Performance / Cost:
  - Run a 1-hour perf job against Dedicated configs A/B (quantized vs non-quant) and attach the cost-per-token delta.
  - If latency regression >10% p95, schedule a profiling session (perf owner + model infra).
  - Add a note to the Optimize backlog for a suggested batching tweak.

- Reliability / Rollbacks:
  - If we had any 5xx increases >2x baseline, mark for immediate rollback and incident review.
  - For fallback rules added to runtime, add an automated canary that sends 1% of traffic for 2h then ramps.

Action templates (copy-paste into PR comment or Jira):
- Quick follow-up (owner: NAME): "Add unit test for XYZ input and attach sample failing input. Blocker? No. Estimate: 1d."
- Investigate perf (owner: NAME): "Run A/B perf run with quantization profiles, capture p95 and cost per token baseline vs current. Add results to RD ticket. Estimate: 3d."
- Docs update (owner: NAME): "Update API quickstart and add changelog entry. Estimate: 0.5d."

Owner assignment rules:
- If PR author is the feature owner, they own docs & tests unless they explicitly assign.
- Observability / perf work defaults to eng-sre or perf team; assign to oncall if urgent.
- If action touches public SDK surface, tag the SDK owner (@sdk-leads) and set due date = next release cut.

Automation ideas (notes to self):
- Bot that runs this heuristic and appends a templated follow-up checklist in PR description on merge.
- When PR merged, create a short ephemeral tag in logs and a dashboard row that auto-populates for 24h.
- Auto-create RD ticket if any post-merge monitor fires at >2x baseline within 2h.

Signals to watch (observability checklist):
- Error rate: 5xx and client error spikes; break down by route and model.
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 for all affected routes (compare last 24h baseline).
- Token cost: tokens/sec and cost-per-token delta.
- Cold start frequency for Dedicated pools.
- Unexpected Redis/KV miss rates if cache changes were involved.

Open questions / hypotheses I keep jotting down:
- Is 2h post-merge window sufficient for model-related regressions? My hunch: no, need 24h for traffic patterns. Put this as a configurable parameter for the bot.
- How to make ownership sticky when a PR touches multiple teams? Maybe a primary + secondary owner model.
- Should we automatically label follow-ups "quick" vs "investigate" based purely on code churn heuristics? Risky — false positives.

Examples (copy from live) - useful to paste into new PRs:
- GH PR 4582: Runtime fallback for long-context requests. Followups created: RD-2378 (perf investigation), RD-2421 (docs update). Observability tag: pr:4582. Outcome: perf regression identified (p95 +12%%), small batching change fixed it.

Personal TODOs (for this doc):
- Build the first version of the bot that posts the template on merge (prototype: write a GH action + tiny lambda).
- Add this doc to the eng handbook under "post-merge processes".
- Run a 2-week trial where we require explicit follow-up assignment for every merged PR touching service code.

Notes to self (style):
- Keep follow-ups as small, actionable items (prefer single-responsibility).
- Avoid vague phrases like "investigate later" — assign a 1-sentence goal and an estimate.

Recent snippets to copy into PRs:
- "Post-merge followup: create RD ticket for perf run (attach pre/post graphs). Owner: @Mina. ETA: 72h."
- "Add log tag 'pr:4582' for 24h. Owner: @Jordan. ETA: 2h."

Endnotes:
This is a living scratchpad. If it looks useful, I'll convert to a template and wire up into our GH merge pipeline. Keep small, keep assigned, keep measured.
